races.name: Fenchurch Insurance Brokers Handicap

runners_data.name: The Thames Boatman
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who starts slowly but showed improved turf form in headgear last month, faces tactical challenge with likely soft pace
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple AW winner; quirky sort who often starts slowly but he finally got off the mark (in a change of headgear) on turf in 5f Goodwood handicap last month; up 3lb but he can make his presence felt again.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who went too freely from wide draw last time, needs to settle better but course winner when right
runners_data.spotlight: C&D scorer; not seen to best effect on his last three runs since scoring at Wolverhampton (5f) in March, going too freely from an outside draw when last of six at Bath (5f) last time; interesting from an easing mark.

runners_data.name: Mesaafi
runners_data.note: Only confirmed pace-setter wearing blinkers, gets uncontested lead but question marks over finishing kick on 31-day break
runners_data.spotlight: On a losing run but he got right back on track with fourth of 17 in handicap at Ascot (5f) last month; can go well off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Wheels Of Fire
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning to winning venue but disappointing since April victory, needs stronger pace to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: Resumed winning ways at Musselburgh (5f) in April but below form all three runs since, fourth of six at Haydock (5f) 11 days ago; this course winner is handily weighted if back on his A-game though.

runners_data.name: Diomed Duke
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in tongue-tie making seasonal return after 223-day break, fitness unknown but good course record
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Lingfield (5f, AW) last June and signed off with a good third of ten in 5f Yarmouth handicap in October; in the mix if fully tuned up for his seasonal return.

runners_data.name: HK Fourteen
runners_data.note: Course winner who should strip fitter after recent pipe-opener, prominent style suits if pace is reasonable
runners_data.spotlight: A three-time winner (including over C&D) in 2025; off six months before a fading tenth in 6f Doncaster handicap on his recent return and he should strip sharper here.

runners_data.name: Solar Edge
runners_data.note: Front-running winner last time who may have to settle behind Mesaafi, proven at the trip with strong recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Made light of a five-month absence when making all in 5f handicap at Bath 35 days ago, holding on by a nose from The Thames Boatman; not taken lightly despite a 3lb rise.

runners_data.name: Cressida Wildes
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare in visor who struggled badly last time after break, needs to prove Bath runs were not one-offs
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Wolverhampton (5f) in February, but she was off for ten weeks before beating only one in 5f handicap at Ascot 23 days ago; has a bit to prove now.

races.paceDynamic: Mesaafi is the only confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the outset without pressure, creating a sustainable gallop over this flat 5f course. The prominent runners HK Fourteen, Diomed Duke, and Solar Edge will track just behind, while the hold-up specialists The Thames Boatman, Moulin Booj, Wheels Of Fire, and Cressida Wildes will need Mesaafi to keep honest fractions. With good-to-firm ground favoring quick early speed and only one horse committed to making the running, this race shape strongly favors prominent racers who can position close to the pace and kick from the 2f pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Mesaafi gets an easy lead with soft fractions through the first 2f
scenarios.body: The pace-setter maintains control throughout while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on quick ground. Prominent trackers get first run but cannot peg back the leader who has saved energy early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners position perfectly and Mesaafi's fractions are steady but catchable
scenarios.body: Solar Edge, HK Fourteen and Diomed Duke get ideal trips tracking the leader before unleashing finishing kicks. The pace proves just strong enough to blunt Mesaafi's finishing effort while keeping hold-up horses too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surges
scenarios.trigger: If Mesaafi sets stronger fractions than expected under pressure from prominent runners
scenarios.body: The early pace becomes genuinely testing, setting up a finish for the closers with The Thames Boatman and Wheels Of Fire finding gaps late. Quick ground aids their acceleration from off the pace as the early leaders tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If there's significant early interference or traffic problems affecting the principals
scenarios.body: Pace dynamics become irrelevant as key contenders lose position or momentum through no fault of their own. An unfancied runner gets a dream run through to capitalize on others' misfortune.

watchPoints.text: Mesaafi could steal this if allowed to dictate soft fractions without any pressure from the prominent runners early
The Thames Boatman's slow-starting tendency becomes crucial if Mesaafi gets away with an easy lead on good-to-firm ground
Solar Edge's ability to settle behind Mesaafi rather than make her own running will determine if she can repeat Bath success
Diomed Duke's fitness after 223-day layoff is the key unknown given his strong course record and ideal racing weight
Watch for early positioning of HK Fourteen and whether he can overcome his tendency to fade when not getting perfect trips

races.name: Pourou Garhigh Anniversary EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (EBF Qual') (GBB Race) (Div I)

runners_data.name: Lola
runners_data.spotlight: 7,000gns foal, 42,000euros yearling; half-sister to three winners, notably King Cuan (Group-placed 6f/7f; RPR 112); dam, 7f winner (RPR 85); this Caturra filly appeals on paper so enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Bossy Angel
runners_data.spotlight: £11,000 yearling; Pinatubo filly; dam unraced half-sister to smart winners Asjad (6f/6.5f) and Blue Storm (5f); the betting can prove an accurate guide for this newcomer.

runners_data.name: Chianti
runners_data.spotlight: 20,000gns yearling; dam, unplaced over 6f-8.6f (RPR 59), is a half-sister to 1m1f/1m3f Flat and 2m2f/2m3f hurdle winner Bruant; yard is going well with its juveniles so this Tasleet filly rates an interesting newcomer.

runners_data.name: Lion Of Persia
runners_data.spotlight: 40,000euros yearling; dam unraced half-sister to winners Spice Route (US 8.5f Grade 2) and Zurbriggen (useful 7f) out of an Italian Oaks winner; this son of Persian Force can't be ruled out on his first run.

runners_data.name: My Boo Boo
runners_data.spotlight: Ten Sovereigns colt; half-brother to 1m/1m1f winner Salam Dubawi (RPR 93); dam unraced sister to 1m2f/11.4f winner Placidia; market can guide.

runners_data.name: Emirates Express
runners_data.spotlight: Earthlight gelding; half-brother to four winners, notably Goldinthesea (1m; RPR 96); dam Listed-placed 7.4f winner (RPR 97); a noteworthy newcomer, especially if the market vibes are positive.

runners_data.name: Envision
runners_data.spotlight: 5-1 and green, made an encouraging start when a keeping-on fourth of ten in maiden at Thirsk (5f, good) 16 days ago; this Mohaather filly can build on it over this longer trip; blinkers added.

runners_data.name: Ventura Power
runners_data.spotlight: 16-1, hinted at promise when sixth of 12 in maiden here (6f, good to firm) on his debut nine days ago; this son of Perfect Power can build on it for good yard.

runners_data.name: Emerald Bay
runners_data.spotlight: Son of Bayside Boy who has offered little in a pair of 6f Wolverhampton novices this spring; lots more is needed.

runners_data.name: Minnie Bear
runners_data.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica filly; well held (over 5f) in Wolverhampton maiden and Yarmouth novice this spring; needs to take a big step forward.

races.name: Pourou Garhigh Anniversary EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (EBF Qual') (GBB Race) (Div II)

runners_data.name: Space Dreamer
runners_data.spotlight: £9,000 yearling; Space Traveller filly; half-sister to Czech 5f-7f winner Rabbit Zoustar; dam, placed over 6f (RPR 78), is a half-sister to Canadian 1m4f Grade 1 winner Wigmore Hall and US 1m1f Grade 1 winner Ocean Road; possibilities on her debut.

runners_data.name: Good Fighter
runners_data.spotlight: £50,000 yearling, £22,000 2yo; half-brother to winners Jumbeau (Listed-placed 5f; RPR 94) and Sands Of Dubai (7f; RPR 60); dam, 7f AW winner (RPR 76), is out of US 1m winning sister to 1m/1m1f Grade 2 winner Justwhistledixie; this son of A'Ali needs considering, especially if the market vibes are positive.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Dawn
runners_data.spotlight: 26,000euros yearling, 3,000gns 2yo; Coulsty colt; half-brother to 5f winner End Of Story (RPR 90); dam, unraced half-sister to winners Inverleigh (5.7f Listed) and Setarhe (Group-placed 6f 2yo), is out of an unraced half-sister to German 1m2f Group 1 winner Ransom O'War; the betting should prove an accurate guide for this newcomer.

runners_data.name: Uncle Frank
runners_data.spotlight: 1,000gns yearling, £20,000 2yo; dam, 5f winner (RPR 78), is a half-sister to 9.4f/1m2f winner Shaheen Saqaar, out of German 7f Listed winner; stable's juveniles are going well so this Ardad colt is a likely player starting out here.

runners_data.name: Belardo Ace
runners_data.spotlight: 16-1, hinted at promise with a debut fifth of nine in novice at Salisbury (5f, good) nine days ago; this son of Belardo is in very good hands and can take a step forward.

runners_data.name: Dowman
runners_data.spotlight: Sioux Nation colt who has shaped with promise this spring when runner-up in 5f novice at Bath and then 5.5f maiden at the same course, weakening late on latter occasion; big shout back at 5f with tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.spotlight: 66-1, well-held fifth of seven in novice at Bath (5f, good) on his debut 20 days ago; lots more is required from this son of Soldier's Call.

runners_data.name: Fly Test
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1, well-held 11th of 13 in novice at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) on his debut 17 days ago; this son of Bungle Inthejungle should have learned from the experience.

runners_data.name: Arcadian Days
runners_data.spotlight: Lope Y Fernandez filly; well held in a pair of 5f novices at Redcar and Thirsk this spring; significantly more is required.

runners_data.name: Alpaca's Bullet
runners_data.spotlight: Daughter of Soldier's Call still looked green when a never-dangerous seventh of ten in 5f Yarmouth novice 12 days ago; can do better in due course.

races.name: Ravens Roofing Supplies Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Red Legs
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; dam twice-raced half-sister to winners Annie Salts (5f), Flashy Diva (6f 2yo) and Mister Mackenzie (German/French/Belgian 6.5f-8.5f); probably best watched on debut; stable also runs Rianka.

runners_data.name: I Can Dream
runners_data.spotlight: 20,000gns yearling; dam multiple 5f winner (including 2yo/AW; RPR 90), half-sister to winners Dont Have It Then (6f) and Clem A (1m-1m2f), out of 5f-7f winner; stable's horses usually better for a run.

runners_data.name: March Of Time
runners_data.spotlight: 70,000euros foal; closely related to 1m2f turf/1m4f AW winner Time To Blossom (RPR 89), half-sister to three winners including Repeater (7f-1m4f including 2yo; 112) and All Out (Group-placed 5f/6f 2yo; 102); dam 1m winner (74); bred to appreciate further in time but still respected on debut in an uncompetitive race, especially if backed.

runners_data.name: Material Girl
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to six winners including Ken Colt (5f/5.5f including 2yo/Listed; RPR 111), Shot In The Dark (5f-7.5f including AW; 102), Acapulco Gold (5f 2yo Listed; 102) and Media Shooter (6f/7f including 2yo/AW; 93); dam Group-placed 5f winner (102); appealing pedigree and market support should be heeded.

runners_data.name: Name The Day
runners_data.spotlight: 15,000gns yearling; half-sister to winners Wedding Date (5f/6f including 2yo/AW; RPR 93), Amicia (French 7f; 75) and Secret Potion (5f/6f including 2yo/AW; 74); dam placed 6f AW (53), out of 7f 2yo Group 3 winner; worth a market check, but other newcomers appeal more on breeding.

runners_data.name: Gold Digger
runners_data.spotlight: Both runs over 6f on good to firm ground, making a successful debut at Yarmouth (9-4) in May last year (form worked out well) and finishing sixth of 17 in the Albany at Royal Ascot (7-1); the latter was a creditable performance given a slow break and then taking a good hold; this looks a good opportunity on her return, even under her penalty.

runners_data.name: Ventana
runners_data.spotlight: Out of the frame in both starts over 7f, firstly at Newmarket (good to firm) last August and at Lingfield (AW) in January; returns from another absence, but the drop in trip may suit.

runners_data.name: Lady V
runners_data.spotlight: Well held in two starts over 6f seven months apart, the latest on stable debut at Salisbury (good) nine days ago; plenty more needed.

runners_data.name: Viennetta
runners_data.spotlight: Well held in both starts, at Bath (5.7f, firm) and Brighton (5f, good) for Jamie Osborne last August (hooded each time); makes her stable debut (same owner) after nine months off; probably best watched.

runners_data.name: Rianka
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in both starts, over 6f at Southwell (AW) and Lingfield (good) during the spring; major improvement needed.

races.name: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Jel Pepper
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven course form who should benefit from a strong early pace setup
runners_data.spotlight: Saw off 25 rivals when winning a 7f sales race at Newmarket last October (good ground); two defeats in Listed company this year (1m, AW and 7f, good to firm) and now drops back to 6f; well drawn for his handicap debut but this mark not an obvious gift.

runners_data.name: The Untamed
runners_data.note: Front runner in excellent form but faces Comical Point in a potential speed duel that could compromise both
runners_data.spotlight: Confirmed the promise of his Chelmsford debut when running away with a Ripon novice in April; made hard work of defying his penalty at Doncaster 16 days ago, hanging left under pressure, but he was strong at the finish; still has potential and he's one to take seriously on this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Egoli
runners_data.note: Returns after 226 days off and stalls issues at Newbury, but prominent style suits if sharp enough
runners_data.spotlight: Won a maiden and a novice last summer before coming up short in stronger company; gelded over the winter; withdrawn after getting upset in the stalls at Newbury last month (6f Listed; 40-1 at the time of withdrawal); this should be more suitable but others bring stronger claims.

runners_data.name: Lara Antipova
runners_data.note: Improved filly whose prominent style and light weight make her dangerous in the right scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Finished second in her first two starts before readily accounting for four rivals at Lingfield seven weeks ago (6f, AW); open to improvement but it will be needed if she is to defy this mark now handicapping.

runners_data.name: Atticum
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping up to 6f from 5f sprints, needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: All runs at 5f; improved with each 2yo start, winning a Yarmouth novice (good to soft) in October; tapped for speed on his seasonal/handicap debut at Sandown in April, but he was keeping on well close home and the step up to 6f could prompt further progress; ground faster than good will be a first.

runners_data.name: Comical Point
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader who risks getting into a damaging early battle with The Untamed
runners_data.spotlight: Useful 2yo, highly tried after his winning debut at Salisbury; third in his two runs this year, latterly in a Newmarket handicap last month (6f, good to firm); drawn wide but likely to give it another good go.

runners_data.name: River Spey
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 89 days off, needs everything to fall right from the back
runners_data.spotlight: Had some good form in defeat prior to landing an AW maiden last October (6f; 1-4 favourite); not at his best at Kempton in March but this mark is in range judged on his fourth at York's Ebor meeting.

runners_data.name: Amorim
runners_data.note: Prominent type wearing tongue tie, returning to course and distance of his only win
runners_data.spotlight: His 2yo win came in good style over C&D but he was the red-hot favourite; his limitations have been exposed since and he was beaten 8l on his return to action in April (7f, good); returns to 6f with a tongue-tie and blinkers fitted; not easy to assess.

runners_data.name: Mo Of Cairo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose style suits but recent form suggests he needs to bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive 2yo, rounding off 2025 with a fine second at York's Ebor meeting (6f, good to firm); only sixth in his two starts this year but he has not been ridden as prominently as last year; on a good mark and a revival could be forthcoming.

runners_data.name: Nuevo Slovo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping significantly in grade after poor seasonal return at York
runners_data.spotlight: Good sixth in last season's Windsor Castle Stakes at Royal Ascot; 50-1 for last month's stable/seasonal/handicap debut at York and finished well beaten; dropped 4lb but not easily recommended.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Hard Spun
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who must improve dramatically on her poor Newmarket reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice over 6f as a 2yo, including an Ascot nursery off 4lb lower; she needs to leave her Newmarket reappearance well behind if she is come out on top this time.

races.paceDynamic: Comical Point and The Untamed are both confirmed front runners who will contest the early lead in this 6f sprint. With two keen pace-setters likely to engage, an honest gallop is virtually guaranteed from the start. The sustained pace will test stamina reserves and create a strong tempo that should favor horses with tactical speed who can sit just behind the leaders. This race shape strongly favors prominent racers and those with finishing kicks, while pure front runners face the danger of burning out against each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dual Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Comical Point and The Untamed engage in a speed duel from the gates
scenarios.body: The two leaders will set unsustainable fractions and tie up in the final furlong, allowing prominent runners to sweep past. Horses like Jel Pepper and Egoli, who can track the pace without getting involved early, will benefit from the setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If The Untamed gets first run and Comical Point settles behind or vice versa
scenarios.body: The lone leader controls the tempo and has enough left to hold off challengers, with the pace honest but not suicidal. The winner comes from whoever establishes the early advantage cleanest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly frantic and prominent runners also get caught up
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will stretch the field and create gaps for late-running types to exploit in the final 1f. Horses with finishing speed who stay away from trouble will find clear runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Win
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys on the leaders show restraint and create a more tactical affair
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more manageable allowing horses in the first four to kick clear, with tactical speed being the key weapon. Those best positioned turning for home will dominate.

watchPoints.text: Comical Point and The Untamed could engage in a destructive early speed battle that compromises both horses
Egoli's lengthy absence and previous stalls issues at Newbury make his participation uncertain until the gates open
Atticum steps up in distance from 5f to 6f for the first time, testing whether he has the stamina for the trip
River Spey and Nuevo Slovo both return after lengthy breaks and need to prove their fitness first time back
The good to firm going may favor those with proven form on similar surfaces like Jel Pepper and The Untamed

races.name: Don & Low Champions Cup 2026 Handicap

runners_data.name: Stintino Sunset
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to form after 25 days off, consistent performer who needs pace to aim at
runners_data.spotlight: Just 3-44 but she is consistent and has winning form over C&D; was returning from 87 days off when beaten about 4l into fourth of 11 behind Moon Over The Sea here last month and should finish closer on 5lb better terms; new headgear combination.

runners_data.name: Graffiti
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing first-time blinkers, needs them to spark improvement on declining handicap mark
runners_data.spotlight: Has caught the eye a couple of times recently, but isn't proving easy to win with despite a declining mark; needs first-time blinkers to make a difference.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Only confirmed pace-setter, key advantage but may need further than this trip now
runners_data.spotlight: Drops in grade and now 2lb below her last winning mark, but well beaten in both starts since returning in April; probably needs further than this now.

runners_data.name: Gert Lush
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up horse coming off a narrow defeat, 23 days since last run freshens him up
runners_data.spotlight: Had dropped 11lb lower than when last successful when beaten a neck at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm) last month (third and fourth have won since); races off the same mark, but she didn't get home in one previous attempt over this far.

runners_data.name: Moon Over The Sea
runners_data.note: Strong recent form including course and distance win, hold-up style suits if pace develops
runners_data.spotlight: Still 4lb higher than when winning over C&D (good to firm) last month, but has run well off this mark and higher in her two outings since; has finished first and second in his two starts under Myla Coppins; stable also runs Dogged; major player.

runners_data.name: Lynda's Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 261 days off, fading tendency makes her vulnerable late
runners_data.spotlight: Huge prices and didn't beat many in three starts over 1m/1m2f last year; makes her handicap debut after seven months off; best watched unless backed.

runners_data.name: Dogged
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making stable debut after 216 days off, market will indicate expectations
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time winner on turf, but losing run now up to 21; makes his debut for another new yard after seven months off and the market should indicate what is expected.

runners_data.name: Guinness Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed ability when second here nine days ago, takes strong hold
runners_data.spotlight: 0-18 but does possess ability as when second of 15 on his return from four months off here (1m2f, good to firm) nine days ago; usually takes a good grip, though, and this sort of trip has found him out in the past.

runners_data.name: Just Adair
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course and distance wins, tongue tie helps and 216-day break may refresh
runners_data.spotlight: Tongue tied all starts; won his first two handicaps, over C&D (good to firm) last August/September, and a below-par effort on her final outing was probably down to the soft ground; returns from seven months off and the market should be most informative.

runners_data.name: Scammer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making turf debut in visor, poor all-weather form offers little encouragement
runners_data.spotlight: Huge prices and no worthwhile form in five starts over 7f-1m6f on the AW; visor given a go this time, but makes little appeal on turf debut after another 80 days off.

runners_data.name: Launceston
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has shown nothing in five starts for current yard, hard to fancy
runners_data.spotlight: 0-13 under rules; runner-up in one of his nine starts for Sir Mark Prescott, but has shown nothing in five outings for this stable, four of them over hurdles.

races.paceDynamic: Regally Blonde is the only confirmed front runner in this 11-runner field, likely to dictate terms without serious pressure from the start. Just Adair and Dogged may sit prominently, but most of this field comprises hold-up horses including Moon Over The Sea, Gert Lush, Stintino Sunset, Graffiti, Guinness Lad, and Scammer. With minimal early pace pressure, Regally Blonde can control fractions and potentially steal a march on the patient types who will need to make ground from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and early pace-setters who can capitalise on the lack of speed pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Regally Blonde gets soft fractions without serious pressure
scenarios.body: She can dictate ideal splits and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still organising their runs. The lack of pace pressure allows front runners to conserve energy for a strong finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get their ideal scenario with a strong gallop in the final three furlongs. Moon Over The Sea and Gert Lush can unleash their finishing kicks when it matters most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Just Adair or Dogged track Regally Blonde closely and pounce late
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get the best of both worlds, saving ground behind the leader while staying close enough to strike. They avoid the traffic issues that often plague hold-up horses in small fields.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Regally Blonde goes too slow and multiple horses make simultaneous moves
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy scramble where any horse with a turn of foot can capitalise. Fitness and recent form become crucial as horses bunch up in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Just Adair shows early pace to pressure Regally Blonde, could create the tempo this field needs
Monitor Guinness Lad's early positioning as he usually takes a strong hold and may get involved sooner than intended
Check Dogged's market support as stable debut after seven months off makes him hard to assess
Observe if Moon Over The Sea gets the patient ride her hold-up style requires or if connections force the issue
Watch for early pace development as Regally Blonde's uncontested lead could prove decisive in this weak pace scenario

races.name: Marley Solar Roof System "Confined" Handicap (For horses Which Have Not Won More Than One Race)

runners_data.name: Bennyworth
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making turf debut after five AW starts, solid handicap form but needs to prove surface switch works
runners_data.spotlight: All five starts on the AW, faring best when second of six on handicap debut at Lingfield (1m) in April (winner has gone in again twice since); has a bit to prove up in trip on turf debut, though.

runners_data.name: Kalokalo
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with good form at this trip, neck second at Newbury suggests competitive off current mark
runners_data.spotlight: Mainly consistent since handicapping, winning at Yarmouth (1m, good to soft) last September and beaten only a neck and a nose into third of 14 at Newbury (1m2f, good) last month; major player off just 1lb higher.

runners_data.name: My Champion
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won on AW but disappointing in headgear since, needs to recapture January form
runners_data.spotlight: Seven starts on the AW including a narrow success at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in January, but has not matched that form in two outings in headgear since; enough to prove on turf debut.

runners_data.name: African Gib
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning after 180-day break with step up to handicap debut trip, market check essential
runners_data.spotlight: Modest in three starts over 1m on turf/AW late last year, but may improve now upped in trip for his handicap debut after six months off; worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Zoustellar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with winning form at this distance in cheekpieces, disappointed last time but has scope to bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Responded well to cheekpieces when off the mark at Yarmouth (1m, good) in April, but disappointed at Bath (1m, firm) later in month; needs to bounce back, and her pedigree raises stamina doubts.

runners_data.name: Salamis Bay
runners_data.spotlight: Some ability in her first two starts over 6f on the AW and faced an impossible task at Ascot (1m2f, good; 125-1) last month; still open to improvement on handicap debut and may show a bit more; non-runner

runners_data.name: Thimble
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced in three starts over 7f on the AW this year, but looks interesting up in trip for her handicap/turf debut given her stamina-laden pedigree on the dam's side; refused to enter the stalls at Nottingham last month.

runners_data.name: Bosom Pals
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to form after long break, won over 7f and this trip extension could suit
runners_data.spotlight: Narrowly made a successful nursery debut at Thirsk (7f, good to firm) last August and was returning from 254 days off when fourth of seven at Nottingham (1m, good) last month; wouldn't be sure to appreciate the longer trip on breeding.

runners_data.name: We Ride At Dawn
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will get uncontested lead but showed poor form on stable debut 12 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Far from disgraced on her final start for Dominic Ffrench Davis at Kempton (7f, AW) last autumn, but never figured on stable/handicap debut there (1m) 12 days ago; bred to stay, but improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Dijon Gone
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with fade-in-finish concern who was well beaten behind Kalokalo last time
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in her first three starts over 1m and finished about 4l behind Kalokalo on handicap debut at Newbury (1m2f, good) last month; needs to find a bit more.

runners_data.name: Mohaab
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse hitting form with emphatic 1m2f win 13 days ago, 7lb rise may not stop momentum
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark at the tenth attempt with an emphatic success at Nottingham (1m2f, good to soft) 13 days ago; 7lb rise wouldn't stop her if in the same mood, but she could probably do with rain.

runners_data.name: Meritocratic
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer disappointing in four starts but now gelded with visor added for first time
runners_data.spotlight: Out of the frame in four starts, failing to run up to market expectations on handicap debut at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) seven weeks ago; gelded since and a visor is now given a go; interesting to see if his backers return.

races.paceDynamic: We Ride At Dawn is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms unopposed early, setting a manageable tempo over 1m2f on good turf. The prominent runners Bennyworth, Kalokalo and Bosom Pals will track behind without applying serious pressure, while the majority adopt hold-up tactics including Mohaab, Zoustellar and My Champion. This sustainable pace will favour the patient hold-up horses who can quicken late, as the leaders will have energy left to kick when challenged but the deep field of closers creates the strongest finishing threat.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If We Ride At Dawn sets modest fractions without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The patient closers get the perfect setup to unleash finishing kicks in the final 2f. Mohaab's recent emphatic win suggests she's hitting form at the right time while Zoustellar has winning form at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Pays
scenarios.trigger: If Kalokalo or Bosom Pals apply sustained pressure from 4f out
scenarios.body: The early pace quickens enough to blunt the finishing kicks of the hold-up brigade. Kalokalo's consistent handicap form and Bosom Pals' return to form make them the main beneficiaries of forward positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If We Ride At Dawn gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: The leader capitalizes on the uncontested early pace to build a decisive advantage. With most rivals needing to make up ground, We Ride At Dawn could steal a march despite recent poor form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the main fancies fail to fire and an improver emerges
scenarios.body: African Gib's six-month break and step up in trip could unlock improvement, while Thimble's pedigree suggests this longer distance suits. The moderate pace allows these longer shots to get competitive.

watchPoints.text: We Ride At Dawn could steal this if getting uncontested fractions and the field switches off early
Mohaab's 7lb rise after last win could halt momentum but recent form suggests she's still improving
Kalokalo's consistent form at this trip makes her the main danger if prominent tactics work
African Gib needs monitoring in betting after six-month break and significant trip increase
Zoustellar bouncing back from Bath disappointment would make her dangerous given winning form here

races.name: Skyline Roofing Centers Handicap

runners_data.name: Party Island
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer seeking hat-trick with excellent recent Bath form, though carries 7lb penalty for those wins
runners_data.spotlight: Bids for a hat-trick after two wins at Bath (1m2f, firm), beating Galaxy Wonder by half a length on the latest occasion; up another 2lb, but still a big player in his current mood.

runners_data.name: Fast Steps
runners_data.note: Only pace angle with course form and De Sousa booking, though 17-race losing run creates doubt despite drop in grade
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner whose losing run is up to 17 but he had dropped 14lb below his last winning mark when beaten less than a length into third of seven here four weeks ago; respected if building on that.

runners_data.name: Solanna
runners_data.note: Hold-up type showing improved turf form recently, first-time visor applied and Crouch's 5lb claim helps
runners_data.spotlight: 7-32 on the AW and 2-19 on turf, but he has performed well on grass in his last two starts including when chasing home a stablemate at Yarmouth (1m2f, good) 12 days ago after meeting trouble; should run his race.

runners_data.name: Magical Merlin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on long losing run but continues to drop in weights, tongue-tie failed to spark improvement last time
runners_data.spotlight: Continues to edge down the weights, but losing run is up to 19 and the application of a tongue-tie made little difference last time; something to prove on his first attempt over this far.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with AW wins for previous trainer, stable debut encouraging but failed to build on that promise
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins for Adam West including one on the AW in France; encouraging return/stable debut at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in April but didn't build on it at Newbury (1m, good) last month; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form is poor but has dropped to last winning mark, first-time cheekpieces applied
runners_data.spotlight: Last four efforts leave plenty to be desired but has dropped 2lb lower than for the latest of two wins at Nottingham (1m2f) last July; respected if the first-time cheekpieces bring about a resurgence.

runners_data.name: Grey Fox
runners_data.note: Course specialist returning after 313 days off, twice won after absence but this layoff seems extreme even for him
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time winner over 1m/1m2f here; back off his last winning mark and has twice won after an absence, but whether he can do so after 313 days off is a moot point; may also need further than this now.

runners_data.name: Brodie's Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from wind surgery with poor overall record, just 75 days since last run may not be enough
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced on his first start since wind surgery when fourth of seven at Kempton (1m3f, AW) in March, but is just 1-23 and hasn't threatened in just four outings on turf.

runners_data.name: Galaxy Wonder
runners_data.note: Most consistent performer recently with strong Bath second to Party Island, extra 1lb penalty hurts his chances
runners_data.spotlight: Most consistent since joining this yard (314323112) and was only beaten half a length by Party Island in his hat-trick bid at Bath (1m2f, firm) last month; despite that latest effort a bit of rain wouldn't come amiss; stable also runs Brodie's Boy.

runners_data.name: Gretna Dreams
runners_data.note: Hold-up winner at this trip last August but 214 days off and below-par in final two runs of last campaign
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice, over 1m2f at Brighton (good) and Newmarket (good to firm) last August, but below form in her last two outings; only 1lb lower and has fitness to prove after seven months off.

races.paceDynamic: Fast Steps will lead or set the early tempo, likely accompanied by no other genuine pace angles, creating a controlled gallop through the early stages. The moderate pace will suit the army of hold-up horses including Party Island, Galaxy Wonder, and Solanna who can all track the leaders before challenging. With nine of ten runners showing hold-up tendencies and only Fast Steps offering early pace, this sets up perfectly for closers who can produce their best work in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can settle and finish, particularly those with proven tactical speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Fast Steps sets uncontested fractions and the field settles behind him
scenarios.body: The steady gallop allows hold-up horses to conserve energy and produce sustained finishes, with class horses like Party Island and Galaxy Wonder able to time their challenges perfectly. Fast Steps may even stay on if the pace is slow enough, but the in-form closers should have too much firepower.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fast Steps Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If Fast Steps gets very easy fractions and the field is slow to organize behind
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage as the hold-up brigade leaves themselves too much to do in a slowly-run contest. Fast Steps has course form and De Sousa's tactical awareness could exploit the lack of early pace pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle Benefits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If several hold-up horses are caught wide or denied clear runs in the home straight
scenarios.body: The compressed field and lack of early pace creates traffic problems, allowing a horse that races closer to the pace like Solanna or one that gets first run to capitalize. Poor draws or positioning costs the fancied closers crucial momentum.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long Absence Returns
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Fox or Gretna Dreams produces a sharp return despite lengthy layoffs
scenarios.body: Either horse recaptures their best form fresh and benefits from the tactical setup that suits their style perfectly. Their class on their day could overcome the fitness concerns in this moderate contest.

watchPoints.text: Fast Steps could steal this if De Sousa judges the early pace perfectly and builds an unassailable lead over the hold-up brigade
Party Island carries 7lb worth of penalties for his recent wins which could prove costly in what looks a competitive handicap
Grey Fox and Gretna Dreams both return from very long layoffs exceeding 200 days, making their fitness a major question mark
Solanna sports first-time visor and gets Crouch's valuable 5lb claim, suggesting connections expect improved effort
The good to firm going conditions favor Party Island and Galaxy Wonder who both won their recent Bath encounter on firm ground
